newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's Exchequer Returns welcomed by markets.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Exchequer Returns welcomed by markets.

text.p: Irish bonds surged after the release on Wednesday of exchequer returns for end-September showing a surplus of 185 million punts.
Bond dealers said the market had taken the figures very well and expected further gains on Thursday morning.
"I think the figures were very good for the economy. They show that funding is positively very strong at the moment..more gains can be expected tomorrow," one dealer said.
By 0615 GMT, the 8.00 percent bond had risen 90p from Tuesday's close of 107.36 to yield 5.82 percent. It was at 106.96 shortly before the release of the figures.
The 8.00 percent bond due 2006 rose 117p from the close at 108.30 to yield 6.70 percent having been at 107.65 before the release of the data.
Equity dealers said positive sentiment after the data was also feeding through to the equities market.
"The figures had a very positive impact on the Irish financial stocks which have benefitted from a strong bond performance and more gains can be expected tomorrow," one equity dealer said.
The ISEQ index of shares gained over 10 points to 2,675.45 after the data.
On the currency market dealers said the strong Returns should result in a good demand for the Irish pound on Thursday morning.
The Irish pound was at 1.0210 sterling, $1.5990 and 2.4465 marks compared with 1.0207 sterling, $1.5985 and 2.4395 marks at 1130 GMT.
